title: Private Deployment: Network Isolation & Offline Upgrade Acceptance Checklist
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines precise requirements and acceptance criteria for Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments where networking isolation and offline/air-gapped upgrades are required. The goal is to provide an auditable, testable checklist teams can run to validate a customer environment prior to production upgrade windows or qualification for air-gapped SLAs.

Background:
Several Enterprise customers have requested stronger guarantees around upgrades when their deployments are in isolated networks: no unexpected egress, deterministic upgrade paths with image signing, rollback capability, and self-hosted registry support. Existing acceptance docs overlap with other tickets but do not capture an actionable checklist combining networking constraints, upgrade orchestration, and air-gap operations.

Goals:
1) Define network-level constraints and verifiable checks for isolated deployments.
2) Specify upgrade choreography that works both online and offline, including cryptographic image verification and staged rollouts.
3) Provide acceptance tests and diagnostics that field engineering and SRE can run during pre-upgrade validation.
4) Minimize blast radius and provide clear rollback semantics.

Scope (in):
- VPC-isolated and on-prem (air-gapped) deployment configurations supported by Redwood Private.
- Upgrade orchestration flow used by the Private control plane and customer-managed node pools.
- Local registry sync and image signing verification.
- Documentation and automated checks in the Console and CLI for acceptance validation.

Scope (out):
- Cloud-provider-specific networking automation (we define requirements; implementation by infra team).
- Full e2e test harness for every on-prem variant (we provide test scripts and acceptance criteria).

Requirements (networking):
- Outbound Egress Control: By default, nodes must not be allowed direct outbound to the public internet during qualification. If egress is required for image sync, it must be via a dedicated proxy or NAT IP that is documented and allow-listed.
- DNS & Resolver Requirements: Customers must provide resolvers that can resolve allowed hosts; fallback to stub resolver is required. DNS leakage checks must pass (no queries to unexpected domains).
- Time Sync: NTP or equivalent time service must be reachable; upgrades must fail fast if system clock skew > 5s.
- Routing & Firewall Rules: Ports and CIDR ranges required for control plane traffic must be explicitly documented. Acceptance check confirms no other external CIDRs are reachable from control plane.
- Proxy Support: HTTP(S) proxy and TLS intercepting proxies supported; upgrade tooling must support configuring proxy credentials and certificate bundles.

Requirements (upgrade flow):
- Image Signing: All release artifacts must be signed. Upgrade tooling validates signatures against customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) or Redwood provided root when allowed.
- Local Registry Support: Customers can host a synced registry. Upgrade tooling must support registry mirroring (OCI) and manifest digest verification.
- Staged Rollout: Support canary stage, percentage-based rollouts, and automatic health checks. Rollout must support immediate halt on regressions.
- Idempotent Steps: Upgrade steps must be idempotent so retries do not leave cluster in inconsistent state.
- Rollback Path: A tested rollback path to the previous pinned version must be documented and executable without internet access if images exist in local registry.

Requirements (air-gapped constraints):
- Offline Artifacts Bundle: Provide an artifacts bundle (images, manifests, helm charts, crt bundles, migration scripts) that can be transferred via offline media.
- Airgap Verification Mode: Upgrade tooling includes an "airgap-validation" mode that performs dry-run checks against a local registry and local DNS, producing a machine-readable report.
- No Implicit Telemetry: Telemetry/health pings to Redwood endpoints must be optional and off by default in configurations qualified as air-gapped.

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- Networking: Validation script shows zero unexpected external connections during a dry-run upgrade test. Evidence is a connection log and DNS query list.
- Image Integrity: Signed image verification passes for all images used in the upgrade; manifests show signature verified by configured key.
- Local Registry: Upgrade completes using only images from the provided local registry with validated digests.
- Rollout Safety: Canary stage exposed to at least one node pool and health checks pass for 15 minutes; automatic rollback triggers if error rate > 5% or latency SLO breached.
- Airgap Dry-run: airgap-validation mode completes with exit code 0 and produces report.json that includes checks for DNS, registry, image signatures, and time sync.
- Documentation: Runbook for manual emergency rollback is present and linked from Console; acceptance requires runbook reviewed by SRE.

Acceptance tests and diagnostic checklist (commands & expected outputs):
- network-leak-check.sh -> exit 0; output contains no IPs outside allowed list.
- verify-signatures.sh --key <key> -> returns VERIFIED for each artifact.
- registry-mirror-test -> pulls each image by digest from local registry only; network capture shows no outbound to dockerhub/gcr/etc.
- upgrade-canary --simulate -> reproduces canary flow and writes rollout log with success/failure events.
- airgap-validation --report /tmp/report.json -> file exists and contains sections: dns_check, registry_check, signature_check, time_sync

Rollout and maintenance window policy:
- Upgrades to major runtime releases require a scheduled maintenance window and a defined rollback window. Acceptance requires documented maintenance start, expected duration, and a contingency plan.

Operational notes and tradeoffs:
- Tradeoff: Strict egress block increases operational overhead for syncing images; recommend offering a Redwood-hosted sync appliance for customers who cannot run a local registry.
- Tradeoff: Image signing with customer KMS increases integration complexity; provide fallback to Redwood-signed artifacts when customer explicitly opts in.
